loan: A loan application is approved if A loan application passes two checks: (i) the applicant’s loan risk assessment, done automatically by a system, and (ii) the appraisal of the property for which the loan has been asked, carried out by a property appraiser. The risk assessment requires a credit history check on the applicant, which is performed by a financial officer. Once both the loan risk assessment and the property appraisal have been performed, a loan officer can assess the applicant’s eligibility. If the applicant is not eligible, the application is rejected, otherwise the acceptance pack is prepared and sent to the applicant.
goods_dispatch: If goods shall be shipped, the secretary clarifies who will do the shipping. In parallel, the goods can be already packaged by the warehousemen. If you have large amounts, special shipping will be necessary. In these cases the secretary invites three logistic companies to make offers and the secretary selects one of three logistic companies. In case of small amounts, normal post shipment is used. In the same time, a package label is written by the secretary, and a parcel insurance is taken by the logistics department head if necessary. If everything is ready and merged, the packaged goods are prepared for being picked up by the logistic company.
healthcare: The process begins when the Patient develops new symptoms or experiences a deterioration of a pre-existing condition. Depending on the severity of the symptoms, the process branches into either an emergency or non-emergency pathway. For acute severe symptoms, the Patient or the Patient's Family contacts emergency services or presents directly to the Emergency Department. The Emergency Department evaluates the Patient to make a triage decision: the Emergency Department either admit the Patient to the Hospital for urgent care, or the Emergency Department discharge the Patient with treatment recommendations. If discharged, follow-up care is managed by the General Practitioner, or the Patient is referred to Outpatient Cardiology. For mild symptoms or known conditions, the Patient takes the non-emergency route by visiting the General Practitioner. The General Practitioner adjusts or initiates treatment and recommends a specialized evaluation. Alternatively, the Patient can choose a private route and consult directly with Outpatient Cardiology. During the specialized evaluation, Outpatient Cardiology establishes the final diagnosis, prescribes treatment, and sets up periodic follow-ups. However, upon assessing the complexity of the case, Outpatient Cardiology may decide the case is too complex for outpatient care and will recommend admitting the Patient to the Hospital. Once admitted to the Hospital, medical history must be gathered. The Patient provides medical history directly to the Hospital staff; however, in situations where the Patient is unable to communicate, the Family provides the medical history instead. Based on the final diagnosis, the Hospital administers the appropriate medical, interventional, or surgical treatment. Throughout the stay, the Hospital maintains communication with the Family to continuously inform their Family of the Patient’s progress. When treatment is complete, the Hospital prepares the discharge and gives the Patient a discharge summary containing treatment recommendations and a follow-up plan. The process concludes when the Patient submits this discharge summary to the Patient's General Practitioner.
